Is Reddit really the demon it's made out to be?

I don't think so, I look at like this.

Their site could be worth potentially millions of dollars, they've got a golden ticket. However, what makes the site so great is the community and the community isn't going to tolerate some things. They can't just slap an add on every page like business insider or something because people will just leave. So they don't know how to monetize it.

They could essentially mine data and target ads to users like Facebook, I mean people post just as much information as Facebook sans their name.

You also have moderators, who are unpaid volunteers that do a shit town of housekeeping that make the site what it is, so they have to keep them happy somewhat because they help keep everything somewhat bearable or at least nice looking for unique visitors.

It started as a platform for just direct democracy curation of content and evolved into a platform for free speech and community organization and they don't know how to cash that in, it's not profitable because it's actually the perfect platform for getting the word out about corruption and focusing people to act on injustices. Organizing protests, boycotts, etc. Nobody wants to invest in a beast that could potentially turn around and hurt their business or call out their own shady business practices.

So they can either really start pushing gold and selling t-shirts and not all be millionaires, or figure out some way to sanitize the site enough that they might be able to convince somebody that all that traffic can be monetized. Even though they haven't figured out a really lucrative method yet.

The problem with reddit is not the straightforward advertising. That is tolerable and it is ok.

The real problem is things like corporate shilling, astroturfing, suppression of news and discussion, guerrilla marketing and so on.

There are powers which want to influence and steer the conversation itself, these are not just commercial in nature. Since Reddit decided to monetize on its popularity the narrative has been steadily mellowing down and the artificial influence has been growing.

Yeah, a lot of people see how they can use reddit for their own financial gain in ways that reddit itself really can't. And I think they allow that to a certain extent, not obvious shills but I mean, certain kick starters, or startups, or users that say they started a business ("thanks to you reddit!"), because they can point to these examples and say "look, look, at the potential revenue in this user base"

Then there's just people who know how to game the system and are just using reddit as a marketing platform, that play well within the rules so they can't be called out.
